ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: What is given in the figure is the graph of y=f'(x). It can be seen that from x=0 to x=2, the graph is the horizontal line y=3, and the point (2,3) is marked. From x=2 to x=4, the graph is above the x-axis and descends to the x-axis; from x=4 to x=5, the graph is below the x-axis and descends to the marked point (5,-1); from x=5 to x=6, the graph rises back to the x-axis. Then reason: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, f(6)=f(0)+∫_0^6 f'(x) dx. It is known that f(0)=7, so it is necessary to calculate the signed area enclosed by the graph of f'(x) and the x-axis between 0 and 6. On [0,2] it is a rectangle, with area 2×3=6. On [2,4] it is a triangle above the x-axis, with area (1/2)×2×3=3. On [4,5] it is a triangle below the x-axis, with area -(1/2)×1×1=-1/2. On [5,6] it is a triangle below the x-axis, with area -(1/2)×1×1=-1/2. Therefore ∫_0^6 f'(x) dx=6+3-1/2-1/2=8. Thus f(6)=7+8=15.
